affectedSurfaces: decomposer planning and semantic review inputs
hypothesis: Structurally screening and escaping GitHub-authored task source, then marking both the task snapshot and agent-authored decomposition plan as untrusted exposed output, prevents source text from becoming workflow instructions while preserving the exact material needed for decomposition review.

metricsCompared.name: untrusted GitHub-to-decomposer prompt paths
metricsCompared.baseline: GitHub-authored title and comment text could be persisted after a narrow blacklist and later rendered as authoritative raw exposed output to two agents.
metricsCompared.candidate: Both external source fields are structurally screened and escaped; the task snapshot and decomposition plan each render in separate source-labeled untrusted-content blocks.

metricsCompared.name: focused security and workflow regression suite
metricsCompared.baseline: No regression covered blacklist-bypassing semantic instructions or closing-tag and markdown-fence source content across intake and decomposition.
metricsCompared.candidate: 137 focused assertions passed, including explicit detector-bypass, delimiter-escaping, exposed-output validation, and separate decomposer-input assertions; the AGENTS.md ratchet target is restored to its 134-line baseline.

rationale: This is a fail-closed repair for a confirmed injection boundary. Suspicious GitHub source is rejected before task creation, accepted source retains explicit provenance, and every later agent-facing representation is screened and delimiter-escaped. The change preserves reviewer access to exact source material while removing its instructional authority, with focused regressions covering the confirmed bypass and boundary-breaking payload shapes.
